messages:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: PROD ALERT — p99 latency spike on /v1/generate (prod). p95: 1.2s -> 4.8s, p99: 2.3s -> 12.4s. 5xx rate 4.7% in last 5m. Suspected deploy: sha=abc123. Paging @sarah.c @mike_r @oncall-esc

sarah.c: on it. grabbing traces + canary dashboard. linking grafana: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/xyz/latency?orgId=1

mike_r: seeing a bunch of 504s at the gateway too. Any gateway changes with this rollout?

deepak: I pushed a batching-config tweak in canary earlier today. Prod deploy included batching increase from 16 -> 64 in handler config. Might be related.

emily_prod: support queue: a couple customers reporting timeouts & retries. tagging E2 customers: AcmeCo, BlueWave.

sarah.c: tailing pod logs now — running query:```kubectl logs -f deploy/redwood-api -c api | grep -E "deadline exceeded|i/o timeout|504"```

logs show repeated: `context deadline exceeded` and `write tcp <ip>: i/o timeout` around the same time as the p99 spike. Looks like KV cache miss/eviction storm after batching growth.

mike_r: if batching increased concurrent connections to backend caches, that could cause evictions and timeouts. Recommend rollback of the deploy to remove the batching bump. Can do immediate rollback.

deepak: +1 rollback. I can prepare a config revert afterwards, but we should restore prod to stable.

sarah.c: executing rollback now — running:```kubectl rollout undo deployment/redwood-api --to-revision=prev || kubectl set image deployment/redwood-api redwood-api=redwood-api:abc122 --record```

ops-bot: Deploy job started by sarah.c — job id dj-8765. Notifying oncall and runbooks.

mike_r: I started draining problematic pods and instructed LB to stop sending new requests:```aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:... --attributes Key=deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds,Value=30```

sarah.c: rollback finished — rollout status: SUCCESS. Observability: p95 back to ~0.9s, p99 ~1.5s, error rate down to 0.4%. Monitoring window: continuing to observe for 10m.

emily_prod: updating support tickets now: telling AcmeCo + BlueWave that we've identified a transient timeout spike after a deploy and rolled back. ETA for customer follow-up: 15m.

jia: taking post-incident lead for the next 24h. I'll own the postmortem + communications. Adding to the incident board.

deepak: follow-ups I propose: revert batching param change in config repo, add a canary gating rule that holds batching increases until 30m of stable metrics, add KV cache eviction metrics + alert for eviction rate spike, and add a runbook note about blocking batching changes in prod without extra canary shards.

sarah.c: initial incident summary draft: "Timeline: deploy (sha=abc123) -> p99 spike at +3m -> rollback (sha=abc122) -> p99 normalized at +15m. Impact: elevated 5xx/timeouts for ~12 minutes in us-west-2 affecting 2 enterprise tenants and some self-serve traffic. Root cause hypothesis: batching increase caused cache eviction/connection pressure, leading to timeouts." Will post full draft to INC-2026-456.

mike_r: handing off to @jia for postmortem and customer comms. @oncall-esc please keep an eye for recurrence. :thumbsup:

oncall-esc: acknowledged. Creating severity ticket: INC-2026-456 (Sev2). Assigning to jia, sarah.c, deepak.

sarah.c: customer-impact note for ticket: "~2% of requests experienced 5xx/timeouts at peak; duration ~12 minutes; affected regions: us-west-2; affected tenants: AcmeCo, BlueWave; no data loss reported; mitigation: immediate rollback to sha=abc122."

emily_prod: drafting a customer-safe status line: "We experienced transient timeouts following a recent deploy and have rolled back the change. We're investigating root cause and will follow up within 24 hours with details."

jia: I'll coordinate the postmortem and schedule a follow-up doc. Action items assigned: (1) revert batching change (deepak) (2) add eviction metrics + alert (deepak/sre) (3) tighten canary gating for config changes (sre/platform) (4) customer comms (emily_prod/jia).

sarah.c: ops-bot cleared alert: p99 normalized for 15m window. Thanks team. I'll put the rollback commands & timestamps into the ticket and link graphs.

emily_prod: thanks — I'll update affected customers and monitor for replies.

-- end of thread --
